items.item_text: Basic Life Support (BLS) certification - American Heart Association
Current Bachelors in nursing (BSN) or related healthcare field preferred
Completion of Bachelors in nursing (BSN) or related field within three (3) years of hire
Minimum of two (2) years of clinical experience as a Registered Nurse.
Experience in medical-surgical, emergency department, or care coordination.

Act as the central hub for patient flow by leading and facilitating daily multidisciplinary rounds. Coordinate effectively with Care Coordinators, Hospitalists, Nursing Managers, and Physician Advisors to identify discharge barriers and execute timely transition plans

Utilize advanced computer and analytical skills to monitor, manipulate, and report on key performance indicators (KPIs) related to patient flow. Use data-driven insights to identify bottlenecks and implement process improvements in real-time.
Maintain a high sense of urgency to expedite the discharge process, ensuring patients are safely transitioned out of the acute environment as soon as they are clinically cleared.

Facilitate non-clinical logistics for departing patients, including the coordination of transportation via ride-share services, ensuring that every patient has a clear and reliable plan for departing the facility.

Serve as a bridge between clinical staff and administrative leadership. Communicate complex discharge status updates clearly and concisely to ensure all stakeholders are aligned on the patient’s progress toward discharge.
Proactive problem-solver who can think critically to remove obstacles and manage multiple high-priority tasks simultaneously.
Advanced computer skills. Proficient in Electronic Health Records (EHR) and comfortable manipulating datasets to generate throughput reports and analyze clinical metrics.
Exceptional verbal and written communication skills. Proven ability to influence multidisciplinary teams and navigate challenging interpersonal dynamics in a high-pressure environment.
Ability to foster cooperative relationships across all levels of the hospital hierarchy
